cases.event: One summer, the water level at {E} dropped by almost a meter.
cases.q: What most likely caused the water level at {E} to drop?
restate: The water level at {E} dropped, and the question asks why.
Something made the water level at {E} drop during one summer.
cases.answer: Strong evaporation during a heat wave most likely caused the water level at {E} to drop, because the heat turned more of the water into vapor.
cases.sum: the evidence points to strong evaporation during the heat wave as the reason the water level dropped.
cases.myth: The water level at {E} dropped because the fish drank most of the water.
cases.mythClause: the level dropped only on cloudy days
cases.cause: strong evaporation during the heat wave
cases.alt: a leak in the bottom of the pond
cases.altText: Some neighbors suggested that {E} had sprung a leak in its bottom.
cases.patternQ: What pattern connects the weather and the water level at {E}?
cases.patternA: The water level fell quickly during the heat wave and nearly stopped falling once cooler weather returned, so the water level followed the heat.
cases.patternSum: the water level fell during the heat wave and nearly stopped falling once cooler weather returned.

prediction.whyNot: most of the water was lost during hot afternoons

cases.observerNote: The observers measured the water level every morning and evening.

obs.text: For {n0} days in a row, afternoon temperatures at {E} climbed above {n1} degrees Celsius.
exps: days that hot speed up evaporation, so the pond would lose water quickly
the water level dropped during a long stretch of extreme heat, which fits evaporation
a heat wave that long gives the sun plenty of time to turn pond water into vapor

obs.text: A pan of pond water left in the sun beside {E} lost water at about the same rate as the pond.
exps: a pan cannot leak through a pond bottom, so its matching loss shows evaporation alone can explain the drop
this shows the heat removed the water, since the pan lost water the same way
the matching rates tie the pond's loss to evaporation

obs.text: When cooler, cloudy weather arrived, the water level at {E} almost stopped falling.
obs.tag: the level after the weather cooled
exps: the loss slowed as soon as the heat ended, which is what would happen if evaporation were the cause
the drop ended when the heat ended, so the two are linked
once the cause faded, the effect faded with it

obs.text: Divers checked the bottom of {E} and found no cracks or holes.
exps: a leak needs a crack or hole, and the divers found none
this rules out a leak, because the bottom of the pond was solid
with no opening in the bottom, water had no way to drain out

obs.text: Most of each day's drop at {E} happened in the hot afternoon, not overnight.
exps: a leak would drain water day and night at a steady rate, but the drop happened mostly in the afternoon
this rules out a leak, since the loss followed the heat of the day
water that disappears mainly in the afternoon points to the sun, not to a hole
predExps: this directly contradicts the prediction, since most of the water was lost in the afternoon
if the pond lost most of its water at night, the overnight drop would be larger, but it was smaller
the prediction expected a nighttime loss that never appeared
